items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a precision gravimeter spring-mass test stage suspends a load of mass 0.4 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.4 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0392 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam, a 0.8 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m (with a sensor at x = 0.048 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 10 / (2π) = 1.592 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 3.18 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: The acceleration–displacement line shown models a micro-electro-mechanical resonant beam oscillating harmonically at 4 Hz with amplitude 0.03 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at displacement x = -0.0225 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(4) = 25.13 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(25.13)²(-0.0225) = 14.2 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 14.2 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a short optical pulse enters a 1800 m step-index fiber (core index 1.55, cladding index 1.47, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 11.8°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 1800) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 9.30 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.81 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 5.06 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 5.06 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide deployed in an autonomous lidar reference delay spool comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.62) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.51). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 12.6° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.51 / 1.62 ⇒ θ_c = 68.8°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 12.6°) / 1.62, so θ_axis = 7.74°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 82.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

Calculate the angle θ_axis that the refracted ray inside the core makes with the central axis.
workingSteps: n_ext sin θ_in = n_core sin θ_axis ⇒ sin θ_axis = (1 × sin 12.6°) / 1.62.

parts.prompt: Determine the angle of incidence θ_w of this ray on the core–cladding wall normal, confirming that total internal reflection occurs.

items.stem: A monochromatic beam with free-space wavelength 450 nm (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) enters optical diamond (n₂ = 2.42) from dry air (n₁ = 1) at 22° to the interface normal in an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig. Calculate the optical wavelength in optical diamond.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 450 / 2.42 = 186 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 450 / 2.42 to obtain 186 nm (B).

items.stem: On a Foucault-style brass sphere suspension apparatus, a simple pendulum with a 0.35 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.105 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides gT² by 2π instead of 4π².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the rearranged expression for L.

items.stem: In a Galilean laser beam-expander input stage, an upright object of height h_o = 0.02 m is placed at a distance u = 0.08 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.1 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.1) = -10.0 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.1 − 1/0.08 ⇒ v = -0.0444 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.0356 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.1 m and u = 0.08 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.stem: A monochromatic ray in water of refractive index 1.33 is coupled at 14.7° to the axis into a straight 300 m optical fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) during a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide. Calculate the total ray path length inside the 300 m fiber.
items.workedSolution: Inside the core, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 14.7°) / 1.58 ⇒ θ_axis = 12.3°. The total zig-zag geometric path length is L_ray = L / cos θ_axis = 300 / cos 12.33° = 307 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_axis = 12.3° and computes L / cos θ_axis = 307 m (B).

items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.531 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.25 − (1/-0.5313) = 5.882 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.170 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.531 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.170 m (D).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36) at 51° to the normal during a submarine periscope window assembly. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1.36 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 34.2° and θ₁ = 51° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 51°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(51°) = 78.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 34.2°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 78.0° (A).

items.stem: In a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.5 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.475 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.475 = 1.08 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.21 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a precision watch hairspring linear test bench supports a 0.3 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.024 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.3 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.118 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.3 / 25) = 0.688 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.stem: In a resonant Coriolis mass-flow sensor tube, a mass m = 0.4 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.04 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.4 kg, ω = 15 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.08 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.04 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.216 J.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a high-voltage substation optical isolator link, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 16.2°) along a 1800 m step-index fiber of core index 1.49 and cladding index 1.39. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.49 × 1800) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 8.94 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 6.43 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.49 and L = 1800 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: An over-angled ray in water (n_ext = 1.33) is launched at 33.5° to the central axis into a 350 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.52, n_clad = 1.46) during a structural-health bridge sensor lead. At what angle to the cylindrical wall normal does the leaked ray refract into the cladding?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1.33 sin 33.5°) / 1.52 ⇒ θ_axis = 28.9°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 61.1° (< θ_c = 73.8°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.52 sin θ_w) / 1.46, giving θ_clad = 65.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 61.1° and refracts into cladding to obtain 65.7° (B).

items.stem: In an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig, a collimated laser beam of vacuum wavelength 633 nm (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels in distilled water of refractive index n₁ = 1.33 and strikes a flat boundary with dense flint glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.65 at an angle of incidence of 26° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside dense flint glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 633 / 1.65 = 384 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.33 sin 26°) / 1.65, giving θ₂ = 20.7°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 5.31°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 384 nm (with v₂ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.33, θ₁ = 26°, and n₂ = 1.65 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: During optical testing on a clinical optometry phoropter test cell, a 0.036 m illuminated target sits 1.2 m from a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.4 m. Determine the signed image position v under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.4 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/1.2 = -3.333 m⁻¹, so v = -0.300 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.4 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.300 m (B).

items.stem: A straight 60 m step-index optical fiber in a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.54 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.45. Its flat input end sits in water of refractive index 1.33, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 12.4° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.45 / 1.54) = 70.3°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 23.0°. (c) For θ_in = 12.4°, θ_axis = 10.7° and L_ray = 60 / cos θ_axis = 61.1 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1.33 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 10.7° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a vibrometer calibration shaker table moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.05 m and angular frequency ω = 40 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.014 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 40 × √(0.05² − 0.014²) = 1.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.92 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a calibration run of a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture, a 0.8 kg carriage oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.06 m on a spring of stiffness 32 N m⁻¹. Determine the frequency f in hertz.
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(32 / 0.8) = 1.01 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: A precision optical compensator in an interferometric metrology window uses a flat, parallel-sided crystalline zircon plate of thickness 0.06 m and refractive index 1.92 surrounded by distilled water (n₀ = 1.33). An incident ray meets the entry face at 32° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1.33 sin 32° = 0.705 (emergent angle = 32°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.7048 / 1.92) = 21.5°, so Δy = 0.06 tan θ₁ = 0.0237 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0117 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 21.5° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in distilled water and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1.33 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 32°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1.33 × sin 32° = 0.705.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0117 m.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on an interferometric metrology window guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 58° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.92, so θ_c = 49.5°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(58°) = 64.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 1.92.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the crystalline zircon–fused-silica glass boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in crystalline zircon: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(58°) = 64.0°.

items.stem: Engineers timing an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum use a 0.6 kg bob on a 0.55 m light cord swinging with arc amplitude 0.11 m (g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root on L / g.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 50 N m⁻¹ in a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage suspends a load of mass 1.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.8) / 50 = 0.235 m.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: In a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone, an oscillating body of mass 0.5 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 12 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.12 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.096 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.5 × 12² × (0.12² − 0.096²) = 0.187 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 9.58 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a straight 120 m step-index optical fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.52 and a cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.46. A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 8.8° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.52 ⇒ θ_c = 73.8°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 8.8°) / 1.52, so θ_axis = 5.78°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 84.2°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

Calculate the angle θ_axis that the refracted ray inside the core makes with the central axis.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of vacuum wavelength 515 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagates inside dry air of refractive index 1 during a bathymetric laser-ranging tank. The ray meets a planar interface with fused-silica glass of refractive index 1.46 at an incidence angle of 18° measured from the normal. Calculate the refracted angle in fused-silica glass.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 18°) / 1.46 = 0.2117. Taking the inverse sine gives θ₂ = 12.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 12.2° (A).

items.stem: Optometry apparatus in a compact viewfinder negative-lens element positions an illuminated test letter of height 0.045 m at u = 0.9 m in front of a thin concave lens of focal length f = −0.3 m. Apply the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.3) = -3.33 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.9 ⇒ v = -0.225 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.675 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.3 m and u = 0.9 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.stem: Within an undergraduate ray-box bench, monochromatic light enters a parallel-sided polycarbonate polymer window (n₁ = 1.58, thickness 0.045 m) from dry air (n₀ = 1) at 64° to the normal and exits into liquid ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). What is the angle of refraction in liquid ethanol?
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 64°) / 1.36, giving θ₂ = 41.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 41.4° (C).

items.stem: A collimated ray inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65, vacuum light speed c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a flat interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at 50° to the normal during a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon. Through what angle is the ray deviated from its original forward path at this boundary?
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1 / 1.65 gives θ_c = 37.3° and θ₁ = 50° > θ_c, the beam undergoes total internal reflection with θ_r = 50°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 37.3°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 80.0° (B).

items.stem: In a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.8 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.3 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.325 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.3 / 9.81) = 2.29 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.3) × 0.325 = 0.893 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 8.34 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: In a precision marine-chronometer balance-mass rig, a load of mass m = 0.5 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 25 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.032 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.5 × 9.8) / 25 = 0.196 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.5 / 25) = 0.889 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 1.60 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.6 kg, ω = 25 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.04 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.02 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.225 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: A 1200 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a borehole geophysical telemetry line has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.5 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.44 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 14.9°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 1200) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 6.00 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.25 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 2.50 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.5 and L = 1200 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: In an immersion-microscopy optical stage, a collimated laser beam of vacuum wavelength 650 nm (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels in dense flint glass of refractive index n₁ = 1.65 and strikes a flat boundary with fused-silica glass of refractive index n₂ = 1.46 at an angle of incidence of 48° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside fused-silica glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 1.46 = 445 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.65 sin 48°) / 1.46, giving θ₂ = 57.1°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 9.12°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 445 nm (with v₂ = 2.05 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.65, θ₁ = 48°, and n₂ = 1.46 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: The velocity–displacement phase portrait shown represents an ultrasonic surgical transducer tip oscillating with ω = 30 rad s⁻¹ and x₀ = 0.1 m. Find the oscillator's speed at x = 0.028 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.1² − 0.028²) = 2.88 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 2.88 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a 0.36 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.09 m and a measured period of 0.298 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.36) / (0.298)² = 160 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

items.stem: In a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of dense flint glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.05 m) at an angle of incidence of 56° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 56° = 0.829 (emergent angle = 56°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.8290 / 1.65) = 30.2°, so Δy = 0.05 tan θ₁ = 0.0291 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0252 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 30.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 56°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 56° = 0.829.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0252 m.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a gemstone goniometer calibration rig guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside dense flint glass (n₁ = 1.65) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 50° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.65, so θ_c = 37.3°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.65 = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.65.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the dense flint glass–dry air boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in dense flint glass: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.82 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(50°) = 80.0°.

items.stem: A 0.5 kg brass bob on a 1.6 m suspension wire in a geophysical field-survey simple pendulum oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.448 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 1.11 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.29 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 5.29 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

items.stem: In a robotics compliant-actuator test carriage, a 0.2 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of constant 32 N m⁻¹ and executes vertical SHM of amplitude 0.032 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq from the spring's unstretched length.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.2 × 9.81) / 32 = 0.0613 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In a dynamic mechanical thermal-analyzer probe, a 0.15 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.12 m (with a sensor at x = 0.06 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 15 / (2π) = 2.387 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 4.77 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 12 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.08 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.028 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(12) = 75.40 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(75.40)²(0.028) = -159 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -159 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In a high-voltage substation optical isolator link, a short optical pulse enters a 750 m step-index fiber (core index 1.6, cladding index 1.5, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 20.3°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.6 × 750) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 4.00 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 4.27 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.67 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.67 × 10⁻⁷ s (C).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index waveguide deployed in a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.52) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.46). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 8.8° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 1.52 ⇒ θ_c = 73.8°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 8.8°) / 1.52, so θ_axis = 5.78°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 84.2°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

Calculate the angle θ_axis that the refracted ray inside the core makes with the central axis.
workingSteps: n_ext sin θ_in = n_core sin θ_axis ⇒ sin θ_axis = (1 × sin 8.8°) / 1.52.

items.stem: In an immersion-microscopy optical stage, a narrow optical ray travelling in distilled water (refractive index 1.33) meets a polished dielectric block at 48° to the normal and refracts to an angle of 36.8° to the normal inside the block. Determine the refractive index n₂ of the block.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ gives n₂ = 1.33 × sin 48° / sin 36.8° = 1.65.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates n₂ = n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 1.65 (C).

items.stem: On a museum horology restoration pendulum rig, a simple pendulum with a 0.18 kg bob swings through a small arc amplitude of 0.21 m with a measured period of 2.66 s. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the effective length L of the pendulum?

items.stem: Optometry apparatus in a Galilean laser beam-expander input stage positions an illuminated test letter of height 0.036 m at u = 0.16 m in front of a thin concave lens of focal length f = −0.2 m. Apply the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.2) = -5.00 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.16 ⇒ v = -0.0889 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.0711 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.2 m and u = 0.16 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

items.stem: In an industrial laser-welding delivery cable, a 300 m step-index waveguide with n_core = 1.54 and n_clad = 1.45 receives light from air of refractive index 1.00 (shown for a 22.5° ray). Determine the maximum external incidence angle θ_max to the axis that still achieves total internal reflection at the core wall.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5187, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5187) = 31.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.2° (C).

items.stem: Within an immersion-microscopy optical stage, monochromatic light enters a parallel-sided polycarbonate polymer window (n₁ = 1.58, thickness 0.055 m) from dry air (n₀ = 1) at 34° to the normal and exits into fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46). What is the angle of refraction in fused-silica glass?
items.workedSolution: Across parallel planar boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 34°) / 1.46, giving θ₂ = 22.5°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 22.5° (C).

items.stem: On a photovoltaic encapsulant test coupon, the critical angle for total internal reflection of monochromatic light passing from a transparent crystal into fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) is measured to be 37.1° to the normal. What is the refractive index n₁ of the crystal?
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.46 / sin 37.1° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.46 / sin 37.1° = 2.42 (D).

items.stem: In a seismic base-isolation pendulum test frame, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.6 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.532 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.532 = 1.21 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.35 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

parts.prompt: Calculate the period T of the pendulum.
Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.
Determine the tension in the suspension cord as the bob passes through its lowest point.

items.stem: A vertical suspension stage in a spacecraft thruster-valve return-spring test fixture supports a 0.75 kg mass on an ideal coil spring of stiffness 40 N m⁻¹, oscillating vertically with amplitude 0.055 m about its equilibrium position (take g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.75 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.184 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.75 / 40) = 0.860 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.93 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: In a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine, a mass m = 1.2 kg oscillates in undamped simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 25 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.1 m. The parabolic energy–displacement curves are analyzed at displacement x = 0.05 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 1.2 kg, ω = 25 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.1 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.05 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 2.81 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

markScheme.criterion: Adds object distance u and positive real image distance v.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a transoceanic telecommunications link, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 15.9°) along a 150 m step-index fiber of core index 1.58 and cladding index 1.49. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 150) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 7.90 × 10⁻⁷ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 8.38 × 10⁻⁷ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 4.77 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.58 and L = 150 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: During alignment of an avionics fly-by-light data bus, monochromatic light from water (n_ext = 1.33) strikes the entry face of a 120 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49) at 15.6° to the central optic axis. Determine the angle of incidence θ_w at the cylindrical core–cladding boundary relative to its normal.
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1.33 sin 15.6° = 1.58 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 13.1°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 76.9°.

items.stem: Engineers testing a spectrophotometer cuvette wall direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 488 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through distilled water (n₁ = 1.33) onto a smooth synthetic sapphire surface (n₂ = 1.77) at an incidence angle of 26° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside synthetic sapphire, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 488 / 1.77 = 276 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.33 sin 26°) / 1.77, giving θ₂ = 19.2°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 6.77°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 276 nm (with v₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.33, θ₁ = 26°, and n₂ = 1.77 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: A straight 750 m step-index optical fiber in an astronomical echelle-spectrograph feed consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.62 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.51. items.workedSolution: (a) θ_c = arcsin(1.51 / 1.62) = 68.8°. (b) Using n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) gives θ_max = 35.9°. (c) For θ_in = 25.9°, θ_axis = 15.6° and L_ray = 750 / cos θ_axis = 779 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 15.6° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: In an aerial reconnaissance camera test collimator, an upright object of height h_o = 0.008 m is held at a distance u = 0.032 m in front of a thin converging magnifying lens of focal length f = 0.08 m. Use the real-is-positive sign convention (1/f = 1/u + 1/v, m = −v/u).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u = 0.032 m and f = 0.08 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a precision optical-chopper resonant blade measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.1 m and angular frequency 20 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.028 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 20 × √(0.1² − 0.028²) = 1.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.92 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: During stiffness testing on a high-speed pantograph contact-spring test rig, a 0.25 kg mass oscillates horizontally with amplitude 0.025 m and a measured period of 0.740 s. What is the spring constant k?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(0.25) / (0.740)² = 18.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

items.stem: In a submarine periscope window assembly, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of optical crown glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.52, thickness 0.075 m) at an angle of incidence of 44° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 44° = 0.695 (emergent angle = 44°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.6947 / 1.52) = 27.2°, so Δy = 0.075 tan θ₁ = 0.0385 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0244 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 27.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 44°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 44° = 0.695.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0244 m.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a microfluidic refractive-index sensor guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) toward a planar interface with dry air (n₂ = 1) at an incidence angle of 44° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1 / 1.92, so θ_c = 31.4°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(44°) = 92.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.92.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in crystalline zircon: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(44°) = 92.0°.

items.stem: A 0.5 kg brass bob on a 0.72 m suspension wire in a museum horology restoration pendulum rig oscillates with arc-length amplitude 0.18 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Calculate the maximum cord tension at the bottom of the swing.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.72), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.664 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 5.21 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 5.21 N (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

items.stem: A vertical helical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹ in a frictionless air-track glider coupled to a calibrated coil spring suspends a load of mass 1.2 kg that subsequently oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.055 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what was the static extension Δx_eq of the spring at equilibrium before oscillation started?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (1.2 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.118 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, a 0.25 kg mass undergoes SHM with ω = 18 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m (with a sensor at x = 0.015 m). Calculate the frequency f_E at which the kinetic energy completes full cycles.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 18 / (2π) = 2.865 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 5.73 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

items.stem: In an ultrasonic wire-bonding horn tip, a component executes simple harmonic motion at frequency f = 6 Hz with amplitude x₀ = 0.02 m, as represented on the acceleration–displacement graph. Taking displacement to the right as positive, what is its signed acceleration a when x = 0.007 m?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(0.007) = -9.95 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -9.95 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for an avionics fly-by-light data bus test a 240 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.57, n_clad = 1.46, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 17.6°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.57 × 240) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 1.26 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.35 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 9.46 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 9.46 × 10⁻⁸ s (C).

items.stem: A 80 m step-index waveguide deployed in a wind-turbine blade strain-monitoring waveguide comprises a glass core (n_core = 1.6) surrounded by lower-index cladding (n_clad = 1.5). Monochromatic light enters from air (n_ext = 1.00) at an angle of 17.3° to the fiber axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.5 / 1.6 ⇒ θ_c = 69.6°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 17.3°) / 1.6, so θ_axis = 10.7°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 79.3°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

items.stem: Within a precision Abbe refractometer cell, a beam of vacuum wavelength 670 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) strikes a planar liquid ethanol–crystalline zircon interface (n₁ = 1.36, n₂ = 1.92) at 42° to the normal. At what speed does the refracted wave propagate in crystalline zircon?
items.workedSolution: From the definition of refractive index n₂ = c / v₂, the wave speed in crystalline zircon is v₂ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes v₂ = c / n₂ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.92 = 1.56 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: In a coastal lighthouse clockwork escapement pendulum, a small dense bob of mass 0.35 kg hangs on a light inextensible cord of length 2.2 m and swings with small arc amplitude 0.22 m. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the oscillation frequency f?

items.stem: Optometry apparatus in a compact viewfinder negative-lens element positions an illuminated test letter of height 0.045 m at u = 0.72 m in front of a thin concave lens of focal length f = −0.4 m. Apply the real-is-positive sign convention throughout.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.4) = -2.50 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.4 − 1/0.72 ⇒ v = -0.257 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.463 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.4 m and u = 0.72 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

items.workedSolution: Inside the dense flint glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1.33 sin 38°) / 1.65, giving θ₁ = 29.8°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.03 × tan 29.75° = 0.0171 m.

items.stem: A prism assembly in a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage places optical diamond of refractive index 2.42 in contact with liquid ethanol of refractive index 1.36 (take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). A test beam strikes the interface from inside optical diamond at 51° to the normal. Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 2.42 = 0.5620, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.5620) = 34.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.36 / 2.42 to obtain θ_c = 34.2° (B).

items.stem: In a cleanroom nanopositioning flexure stage, a load of mass m = 0.9 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 40 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.055 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.9 × 9.8) / 40 = 0.221 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.9 / 40) = 0.942 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 2.44 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

items.stem: A 2400 m multimode step-index optical fiber in a surgical laser-lithotripsy delivery fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.55 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.47 in air (n_ext = 1.00, shown with a guided ray launched at 17.7°). Take the speed of light in vacuum to be c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.55 × 2400) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.24 × 10⁻⁵ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.31 × 10⁻⁵ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 6.75 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.55 and L = 2400 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: A 350 m step-index optical fiber used in a flexible medical gastroscope bundle has core refractive index 1.57 and cladding refractive index 1.46. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 20.8° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?

items.stem: Engineers testing a subsea ROV camera viewport test direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 405 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through crystalline zircon (n₁ = 1.92) onto a smooth optical crown glass surface (n₂ = 1.52) at an incidence angle of 30° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside optical crown glass, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.97 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 405 / 1.52 = 266 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.92 sin 30°) / 1.52, giving θ₂ = 39.2°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 9.17°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 266 nm (with v₂ = 1.97 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.92, θ₁ = 30°, and n₂ = 1.52 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: A harmonic oscillator in a marine wave-tank oscillating piston paddle moves with amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m and angular frequency ω = 8 rad s⁻¹. Calculate its speed when passing through displacement x = 0.03 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 8 × √(0.06² − 0.03²) = 0.416 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.416 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A test rig using a silicon MEMS accelerometer proof-mass flexure test model has mass 1.5 kg, horizontal spring constant 160 N m⁻¹, and oscillation amplitude 0.075 m. What is the natural frequency f of the oscillation?
items.workedSolution: Natural frequency f = (1 / 2π)√(k / m) = (1 / 2π)√(160 / 1.5) = 1.64 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps k/m and m/k, computing (1 / 2π)√(m / k) instead of (1 / 2π)√(k / m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports angular frequency ω = √(k / m) in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the period T = 2π√(m / k) instead of frequency f = 1 / T.

items.stem: A precision optical compensator in an ophthalmic lens-blank inspection jig uses a flat, parallel-sided crystalline zircon plate of thickness 0.05 m and refractive index 1.92 surrounded by dry air (n₀ = 1). An incident ray meets the entry face at 44° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 44° = 0.695 (emergent angle = 44°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.6947 / 1.92) = 21.2°, so Δy = 0.05 tan θ₁ = 0.0194 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0208 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 21.2° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 44°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 44° = 0.695.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0208 m.

items.stem: In a spectrophotometer cuvette wall, a narrow monochromatic beam (speed of light in vacuum c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) travels inside synthetic sapphire of refractive index n₁ = 1.77 and strikes a flat boundary with distilled water of refractive index n₂ = 1.33 at an angle of incidence of 65° to the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.33 / 1.77, so θ_c = 48.7°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 1.77 = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(65°) = 50.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.33 / 1.77.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

parts.prompt: Calculate the critical angle θ_c at the synthetic sapphire–distilled water boundary.
State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in synthetic sapphire: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(65°) = 50.0°.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg pendulum bob suspended from a 1.6 m wire in an evacuated bell-jar precision timing pendulum oscillates in SHM with arc amplitude 0.352 m (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the maximum speed v_max of the bob?
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.6), so maximum speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.872 m s⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the horizontal arc amplitude x₀ as a vertical free-fall drop height h in √(2gh).

options.label: C

items.stem: Engineers testing a university mechanics oscillation sled hang a 0.2 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 32 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.2 / 32) = 0.497 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

items.stem: In a magnetic-levitation harmonic test puck, an oscillating body of mass 0.8 kg executes simple harmonic motion with angular frequency ω = 20 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.06 m. What is its kinetic energy E_k when its displacement from equilibrium is x = 0.048 m?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.8 × 20² × (0.06² − 0.048²) = 0.207 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

items.stem: In a railway trackside acoustic-sensing fiber, a short optical pulse enters a 900 m step-index fiber (core index 1.58, cladding index 1.49, n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 22.2°). With c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, calculate the modal time delay Δt = t_max − t_axial at the output end.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.58 × 900) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 4.74 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 5.03 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 2.86 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 2.86 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: In a tethered deep-sea ROV umbilical waveguide, a straight 120 m step-index optical fiber has a core of refractive index n_core = 1.54 and a cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.45. A narrow laser beam in air (n_ext = 1.00) strikes the flat entry face at θ_in = 15.9° to the central axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.45 / 1.54 ⇒ θ_c = 70.3°. (b) By Snell's law at the end-face, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 15.9°) / 1.54, so θ_axis = 10.2°. (c) Wall incident angle θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 79.8°, which exceeds θ_c so the ray is guided by TIR.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts θ_axis from 90° to obtain θ_w.

Calculate the angle θ_axis that the refracted ray inside the core makes with the central axis.
workingSteps: n_ext sin θ_in = n_core sin θ_axis ⇒ sin θ_axis = (1 × sin 15.9°) / 1.54.

items.stem: A collimated optical ray of free-space wavelength 650 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) in synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) is incident at 42° to the normal on a smooth liquid ethanol surface (n₂ = 1.36) within a submarine periscope window assembly. Determine the angle of refraction θ₂.
items.workedSolution: By Snell's law, n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, so sin θ₂ = (1.77 × sin 42°) / 1.36 = 0.8709. Taking the inverse sine gives θ₂ = 60.6°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 60.6° (C).

items.stem: To calibrate a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum where g = 9.8 m s⁻², a 0.18 kg pendulum bob oscillates at small arc amplitude 0.0936 m with period T = 1.77 s. Calculate the pendulum length L.

items.stem: In a precision optical-power dioptre verification bench, an upright object of height h_o = 0.045 m is placed at a distance u = 0.27 m in front of a thin diverging lens whose focal length is f = −0.15 m under the real-is-positive sign convention.
items.workedSolution: (a) Optical power P = 1 / (−0.15) = -6.67 D. (b) 1/v = −1/0.15 − 1/0.27 ⇒ v = -0.0964 m. (c) Axial separation between object and virtual image on the same side = u − |v| = 0.174 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes f = −0.15 m and u = 0.27 m into 1/v = 1/f − 1/u.
Subtracts |v| from u because virtual image and object are on the same side of the lens.

workingSteps: Both lie on the input side of the lens, so separation = u − |v| = |u + v| = 0.174 m.

items.stem: Engineers coupling light from air of refractive index 1.00 into a 300 m step-index fiber (n_core = 1.58, n_clad = 1.49, reference beam at 14.3°) for a transoceanic telecommunications link must stay within the acceptance cone. Calculate the acceptance half-angle θ_max in the external medium.
items.workedSolution: At the grazing limit, sin θ_c = 1.49 / 1.58, so inside the core sin θ_axis,max = cos θ_c = √(1 − (n_clad / n_core)²). By Snell's law at the entry face, n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) = 0.5256, giving θ_max = arcsin(0.5256) = 31.7°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses n_ext sin θ_max = √(n_core² − n_clad²) to obtain θ_max = 31.7° (A).

items.stem: In a botanical loupe magnifier bench, a thin converging lens of focal length 0.15 m is used as a simple magnifier so that an object of height 0.008 m forms an upright virtual image 0.0808 m in front of the lens (v = −0.0808 m in the real-is-positive convention). At what object distance u in front of the lens is the object held?
items.workedSolution: For a virtual image in the real-is-positive convention, v = -0.0808 m. Thus 1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/0.15 − (1/-0.08077) = 19.05 m⁻¹, giving u = 0.0525 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes negative v = -0.0808 m into 1/u = 1/f − 1/v to obtain u = 0.0525 m (C).

markScheme.criterion: Uses T = 2π / ω with ω = 30 rad s⁻¹.
Substitutes x₀ = 0.08 m and x = 0.04 m into v = ω√(x₀² − x²).

items.stem: Within a precision Abbe refractometer cell, monochromatic light (vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) propagating in synthetic sapphire (n₁ = 1.77) is incident at 43° to the normal on dry air (n₂ = 1). Determine the critical angle θ_c between these two media.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle θ_c, sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.77 = 0.5650, giving θ_c = arcsin(0.5650) = 34.4°.

markScheme.criterion: Uses sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1 / 1.77 to obtain θ_c = 34.4° (B).

items.stem: In a lecture-hall rigid-ceiling wire pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass m = 0.6 kg suspended on a light cord of length L = 1.9 m oscillates in small-angle simple harmonic motion with arc amplitude x₀ = 0.532 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) T = 2π√(1.9 / 9.81) = 2.77 s. (b) v_max = √(9.81 / 1.9) × 0.532 = 1.21 m s⁻¹. (c) Lowest-point cord tension = m(g + v_max² / L) = 6.35 N.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v_max = ω x₀ = (2π / T) x₀.
Uses T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L at the bottom of the arc.

Calculate the maximum speed v_max of the bob as it passes through equilibrium.

items.stem: In a railway bogie secondary-suspension scale model, a load of mass m = 0.4 kg hangs at rest from a vertical spring of spring constant k = 20 N m⁻¹. It is then pulled vertically downward by x₀ = 0.032 m from equilibrium and released. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) Δx_eq = mg / k = (0.4 × 9.81) / 20 = 0.196 m. (b) T = 2π√(0.4 / 20) = 0.889 s. (c) Maximum net SHM acceleration a_max = (k / m) x₀ = 1.60 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Uses mg = k Δx_eq with g = 9.81 m s⁻².
Evaluates a_max = ω² x₀ = (k / m) x₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static extension Δx_eq of the spring when the mass hangs at rest in equilibrium.
Calculate the period T of the vertical simple harmonic oscillations.
Determine the magnitude of the maximum net acceleration a_max of the mass during the oscillation.

items.stem: A 0.25 kg harmonic oscillator in a piezoelectric laser-mirror dithering stage vibrates with angular frequency 15 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.06 m. Consider its mechanical energy distribution when passing through displacement x = 0.036 m.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes m = 0.25 kg, ω = 15 rad s⁻¹, and x₀ = 0.06 m into E_tot = ½mω²x₀².
Applies E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) or E_tot − ½mω²x².
Sets E_p = ½E_tot to obtain x = x₀ / √2.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical energy E_tot of the oscillating mass.
Calculate the kinetic energy E_k of the mass when its displacement is x = 0.036 m.
workingSteps: E_k = E_tot − E_p = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) = 0.0648 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the positive displacement x from equilibrium at which kinetic energy equals potential energy.

items.stem: In a watchmaker's horological inspection stand, a thin converging lens of focal length f = 0.18 m forms a real inverted image of an illuminated object of height h_o = 0.024 m placed at an object distance u = 0.234 m along the principal axis.
items.workedSolution: (a) 1/v = 1/0.18 − 1/0.234 ⇒ v = 0.780 m. (b) |m| = v / u = 3.33. (c) Object-to-screen separation = u + v = 1.01 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds object distance u and positive real image distance v.

items.stem: During pulse-broadening tests for a wind-turbine blade strain-monitoring waveguide, engineers transmit narrow laser pulses from air (n_ext = 1.00, sample launch angle 9.9°) along a 360 m step-index fiber of core index 1.5 and cladding index 1.44. Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) t_axial = n_core L / c = (1.5 × 360) / 3.00 × 10⁸ = 1.80 × 10⁻⁶ s. (b) Longest guided ray has path L / sin θ_c = L n_core / n_clad, giving t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.88 × 10⁻⁶ s. (c) Modal pulse delay Δt = t_max − t_axial = 7.50 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses t_axial = n_core L / c with n_core = 1.5 and L = 360 m.
Applies L_max = L (n_core / n_clad) to find t_max = t_axial (n_core / n_clad).

items.stem: Engineers testing a deep-ocean optical hydrophone window direct a narrow beam of vacuum wavelength 670 nm (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) through optical crown glass (n₁ = 1.52) onto a smooth synthetic sapphire surface (n₂ = 1.77) at an incidence angle of 38° to the boundary normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) Inside synthetic sapphire, v₂ = c / n₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 670 / 1.77 = 379 nm. (b) By Snell's law, sin θ₂ = (1.52 sin 38°) / 1.77, giving θ₂ = 31.9°. (c) Angular deviation δ = |θ₂ − θ₁| = 6.08°.

markScheme.criterion: Obtains λ₂ = 379 nm (with v₂ = 1.69 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).
Substitutes n₁ = 1.52, θ₁ = 38°, and n₂ = 1.77 into n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

items.stem: A straight 450 m step-index optical fiber in an avionics fly-by-light data bus consists of a core of refractive index n_core = 1.57 and cladding of refractive index n_clad = 1.46. Its flat input end sits in air of refractive index 1.00, and a guided test ray is launched at θ_in = 15.9° to the central axis.

markScheme.criterion: Applies 1 sin θ_max = n_core sin(90° − θ_c).
Finds θ_axis = 10.0° and evaluates L / cos θ_axis.

items.stem: Engineers monitoring a quartz crystal tuning-fork tine measure simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.08 m and angular frequency 30 rad s⁻¹. Determine the speed |v| = ω√(x₀² − x²) at displacement x = 0.064 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 30 × √(0.08² − 0.064²) = 1.44 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 1.44 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: An experimental setup consisting of a structural vibration-isolation test sled on linear bearings has oscillating mass 0.45 kg, spring stiffness 18 N m⁻¹, and horizontal amplitude 0.06 m. Calculate the oscillation period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.45 / 18) = 0.993 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation frequency f = 1 / T in Hz instead of the period T in seconds.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

items.stem: In a subsea ROV camera viewport test, a narrow monochromatic beam in dry air (refractive index n₀ = 1) strikes a parallel-sided block of dense flint glass (refractive index n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.085 m) at an angle of incidence of 32° to the normal and emerges back into dry air on the far side.
items.workedSolution: (a) Snells invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 sin 32° = 0.530 (emergent angle = 32°). (b) Inside the slab, θ₁ = arcsin(0.5299 / 1.65) = 18.7°, so Δy = 0.085 tan θ₁ = 0.0288 m. (c) Perpendicular lateral displacement d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0206 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ₁ = 18.7° and applies Δy = t₁ tan θ₁.
Applies d = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ or (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀.

parts.prompt: State the emergent angle of refraction in dry air and calculate the optical Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀.
workingSteps: Because both outer media have refractive index 1 and the faces are parallel, the emergent angle equals 32°.
Snell invariant = n₀ sin θ₀ = 1 × sin 32° = 0.530.

parts.prompt: Calculate the transverse offset Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ of the ray between the entry normal and exit normal along the slab face.
Hence calculate the perpendicular lateral displacement d between the emergent ray and the original incident ray line.
workingSteps: d = (t₁ tan θ₀ − Δy) cos θ₀ = t₁ sin(θ₀ − θ₁) / cos θ₁ = 0.0206 m.

items.stem: A beam-steering prism assembly on a clinical corneal pachymetry test phantom guides light (c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) inside optical diamond (n₁ = 2.42) toward a planar interface with fused-silica glass (n₂ = 1.46) at an incidence angle of 46° measured from the normal.
items.workedSolution: (a) sin θ_c = 1.46 / 2.42, so θ_c = 37.1°. (b) Because n₁ > n₂ and θ₁ > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs at the interface. (c) Wave speed v₁ = 3.00 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and angular deviation δ = 180° − 2(46°) = 88.0°.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into sin θ_c = n₂ / n₁ = 1.46 / 2.42.
States total internal reflection because the ray is in the higher-index medium with incident angle greater than the critical angle.

State and explain the optical phenomenon that occurs when this beam meets the boundary.
parts.expectedAnswer: Total internal reflection occurs because light travels in the medium of higher refractive index and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
workingSteps: Compare incident angle with critical angle in the optically denser medium to confirm total internal reflection.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deviation of the reflected ray from the incident ray's original forward direction, and find the wave speed in the first medium.
workingSteps: Wave speed in optical diamond: v₁ = c / n₁ = 1.24 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
Angular deviation under total internal reflection: δ = 180° − 2(46°) = 88.0°.

items.stem: In a geophysical field-survey simple pendulum, a pendulum bob of mass 0.15 kg hangs on a light cord of length 1.9 m and swings in small-angle SHM with arc amplitude 0.418 m. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², what is the tension in the cord as the bob passes through its lowest equilibrium point?
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 1.9), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.950 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.54 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.54 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

items.stem: Engineers testing an inertial seismometer calibration trolley hang a 0.75 kg mass from a vertical coil spring (k = 100 N m⁻¹) and excite vertical oscillations of amplitude 0.032 m in a gravitational field g = 9.81 m s⁻². Determine the period T of oscillation.
items.workedSolution: Gravity shifts the equilibrium position without altering effective stiffness k, so T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.75 / 100) = 0.544 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly adds weight mg to spring stiffness k, assuming gravity changes the vertical mass-spring period.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the oscillation amplitude x₀ into a pendulum-style formula 2π√(x₀ / g) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the square root.

items.stem: The parabolic SHM energy graph shown corresponds to a studio loudspeaker voice-coil cone (mass 0.25 kg, angular frequency 10 rad s⁻¹, amplitude 0.12 m). Calculate the kinetic energy E_k at displacement x = 0.072 m.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = ½mω²(x₀² − x²) gives E_k = 0.5 × 0.25 × 10² × (0.12² − 0.072²) = 0.115 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the potential energy ½mω²x² at x rather than the kinetic energy ½mω²(x₀² − x²).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Interpolates energy linearly as E_tot(1 − x / x₀) instead of quadratically as E_tot(1 − x² / x₀²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the total mechanical energy ½mω²x₀² instead of subtracting potential energy at x.

items.stem: During calibration of an atomic-force microscope cantilever tip vibrating at f = 1.5 Hz and amplitude 0.03 m, a laser sensor records an instantaneous displacement x = -0.0135 m. Determine the signed SHM acceleration a at that instant.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(1.5) = 9.425 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(9.425)²(-0.0135) = 1.20 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains 1.20 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates −ωx instead of −ω²x, forgetting to square the angular frequency.

items.stem: Engineers evaluating bit-rate limits for a flexible medical gastroscope bundle test a 1200 m step-index waveguide (n_core = 1.62, n_clad = 1.51, n_ext = 1.00, ray shown at 21.6°). Take c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Determine the multipath dispersion delay Δt between extreme guided rays and axial rays.
items.workedSolution: Axial transit time t_min = n_core L / c = (1.62 × 1200) / (3.00 × 10⁸) = 6.48 × 10⁻⁶ s. At the critical angle sin θ_c = n_clad / n_core, t_max = t_min / sin θ_c = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 6.95 × 10⁻⁶ s. Modal delay Δt = t_max − t_min = 4.72 × 10⁻⁷ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δt = (n_core L / c)(n_core / n_clad − 1) = 4.72 × 10⁻⁷ s (B).

items.stem: A 80 m step-index optical fiber used in a subterranean pipeline temperature-sensing cable has core refractive index 1.49 and cladding refractive index 1.39. A laser ray in air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the center of the flat end-face at θ_in = 14° to the fiber axis. What angle of incidence θ_w does the refracted ray make with the normal to the core–cladding wall?
items.workedSolution: At the entry face, 1 sin 14° = 1.49 sin θ_axis ⇒ θ_axis = 9.34°. Since the core wall is parallel to the axis, its normal is perpendicular to the axis, giving θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 80.7°.

items.stem: During quality testing on a semiconductor immersion-lithography stage, monochromatic light in fused-silica glass (n₁ = 1.46) enters a transparent specimen at an incidence angle of 34° and is refracted to 54.7° relative to the boundary normal. Calculate the specimen's refractive index n₂.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ gives n₂ = 1.46 × sin 34° / sin 54.7° = 1.00.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates n₂ = n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 1.00 (C).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts the sine ratio in Snell's law, calculating n₁ sin θ₂ / sin θ₁ instead of n₁ sin θ₁ / sin θ₂.

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the raw ratio of angles θ₁ / θ₂ in degrees instead of sin θ₁ / sin θ₂.

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 0.95 m and bob mass 0.12 kg in a long-case regulator clock calibration rig executes small-angle oscillations of arc amplitude 0.057 m in a field where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Determine its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(0.95 / 9.8) = 1.96 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 1.96 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Incorrectly includes the bob mass m inside the pendulum period equation.

items.stem: In an optical-bench virtual-image calibration rig, an upright test object of height 0.02 m stands 0.3 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length magnitude 0.2 m (f = −0.2 m in the real-is-positive convention). What is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.2 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.2 − 1/0.3 = -8.333 m⁻¹, so v = -0.120 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.2 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.120 m (B).
